prompt: What does an orchestrator do that Compose on one machine does not?

choices.text: Builds images faster
choices.why: Building is not its job.

choices.text: Keeps the declared state true, across machines
choices.why: Right: replicas, replacements and rollouts.

choices.text: Removes the need for a registry between machines entirely
choices.why: Several machines need a registry even more.

choices.text: Runs containers without images
choices.why: It runs images like everything else.

prompt: Ana killed the container of `shelf.2`. What did Swarm do, and why?

choices.text: Nothing, until Ana ran `docker service update`
choices.why: Nobody ran a command; Swarm acted alone.

choices.text: Restarted the same container, as a restart policy would
choices.why: A new task replaced it; the old one stays listed as failed.

choices.text: Started a new task, since two is not three
choices.why: Right: actual state differed from desired state.

choices.text: Scaled the service down to two
choices.why: The declared count does not change by itself.

prompt: `docker service create` warned that `shelf:1.0.0` could not be resolved to a digest in a registry. What is the risk it names?

choices.text: The service will not start until the image is pushed
choices.why: It started; the warning is about consistency.

choices.text: The image will be deleted
choices.why: Nothing is deleted.

choices.text: The service runs without the image's health check
choices.why: The image has one; the warning is about the name.

choices.text: Nodes resolving the tag to different builds
choices.why: Right: each resolves the tag on its own.

prompt: Why did Ana's services use `--endpoint-mode dnsrr` and no published port?

choices.text: The lab's kernel lacks IPVS, which VIPs and the mesh use
choices.why: Right; on a normal host the defaults work.

choices.text: dnsrr is faster than a virtual IP
choices.why: Speed was not the reason.

choices.text: Published ports are forbidden in a one-node swarm
choices.why: They work on a normal kernel, with one node or many.

choices.text: Overlay networks need dnsrr
choices.why: Overlays use a virtual IP by default.

prompt: To replace one task at a time during an update, use `--update-___ 1`.
How does the image's health check make a rolling update safer?
hint: When does Swarm move to the next task?

choices.text: It makes updates faster
choices.why: It makes them more careful, not faster.

choices.text: A broken version stops after one task, not all
choices.why: Right: Swarm waits for each new task to be healthy.

choices.text: It skips the update delay
choices.why: The delay still applies.

choices.text: It rolls back every update automatically, even good ones
choices.why: Only a failure-action of `rollback` reverts, and only on failure.

prompt: After `docker service rollback`, which image did the service run?
hint: The description before the last update.

choices.why: That was the update being undone.

choices.text: `shelf:latest`
choices.why: No `latest` was ever used.
Right, rolled out the same careful way.

choices.text: None; the service was removed
choices.why: Rollback keeps the service.

prompt: How many replicas did `stack.yaml` ask for `web`?
Match each platform to what it is good at.

pairs.right: Small clusters, Compose files as they are
Almost everything, with the largest ecosystem
A web service with no servers to look after

prompt: Ana's team moves `shelf` from Swarm to Cloud Run. What has to change in the image?
hint: What do all these platforms run?

choices.text: It must be rebuilt for Google's runtime
choices.why: Cloud Run runs OCI images as they are.

choices.text: The health check must be removed
choices.why: Removing it is not required, and `/health` stays useful.

choices.text: It must include a web server
choices.why: `shelf` already is one.

choices.text: Nothing; every option runs the same OCI image
choices.why: Right: where it runs is a separate decision.

prompt: A two-person team runs one web service with spiky traffic and no wish to manage servers. Which fits first?
hint: The first bullet of "How to choose".

choices.text: A container PaaS such as Cloud Run
choices.why: Right: no servers, and it scales with the traffic.

choices.text: A Kubernetes cluster that the two of them run
choices.why: A lot of concepts and operations for one service.

choices.text: Compose on a single server they rent
choices.why: It works, but they must manage the server, and spikes hit one machine.

choices.text: Swarm across three machines of their own
choices.why: Still machines to run, for a team that wanted none.
